# Stage 1 plan — foundations

The goal and exit test are in the [build order](../specs/v1/technical/T10-build-order.md), stage 1. This file breaks the stage into steps small enough for one run to finish several. They are not done one after another: every step whose needs have landed is built at the same time as the others, each in its own lane. The "Side by side" section below says what each step needs. How to do a step is in the [runbook](RUNBOOK.md).

## What this machine can and cannot do

- **Node 24 and git are here. Docker, the Supabase command-line tool and the GitHub command-line tool are not.** Do not try to install them.
- **The local database is PGlite**, real PostgreSQL running inside Node, already a dependency of this repository. Migrations, row-level security and every database test run against it. The same SQL must also run on Supabase's PostgreSQL later, so use nothing PGlite-only.
- **There are no vendor accounts yet.** Supabase, Render, Cloudflare, Resend and Google sign-in each sit behind an interface in `packages/providers` with a local stand-in. The real adapter is written and unit-tested against recorded responses, and marked "not verified against the live service" until the founder supplies an account. That list goes into the stage report.

## Steps

Each step is done when its done test passes, the gate passes, the independent review is closed, and it is committed.

### A. Skeleton

- [x] **1.1 Workspaces.** Turn the repository into npm workspaces as in T2 section 1: `apps/web`, `apps/worker`, `packages/core`, `site`, `ui`, `emails`, `providers`, `observability`, beside the existing `contracts`, `database`, `sports`. Empty packages with a `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` and an `index.ts`. The existing apps and every existing script keep working unchanged. _Spec: T2 §1–2, T-20. Done test: `npm run verify` passes; `npm ls --workspaces` lists them. Model: sonnet._
- [x] **1.2 Strict TypeScript and the test runner.** One shared strict config (T-32). Add Vitest for the new packages; the existing `node --test` suites stay as they are. `npm run verify` runs both. _Spec: T1 §1, T9 §2. Done test: a sample test in `packages/core` runs in the gate. Model: sonnet._
- [x] **1.3 Structure checks.** Automatic checks for: import directions (T-21), modules used only through `index.ts` (T-22), no league named in code (T-27), no SQL outside `packages/database`, no hand-written league addresses (T-34), no secrets in browser code (T-30). Each check has a test that proves it catches a planted violation. _Spec: T2 §2 and §6, T9 §3. Done test: planting each violation fails the gate. Model: opus._
- [x] **1.4 Settings and secrets in one place.** A config module read once at startup, checked against a Zod schema; the app refuses to start if a value is missing. `.env.example` lists every value with made-up contents. _Spec: T-30. Model: sonnet._

### B. The database and the league fence

- [x] **1.5 Migration runner.** Numbered SQL files in `supabase/migrations/`; a runner that applies them to PGlite for local work and tests, and can apply them to any PostgreSQL address later. A check rejects a migration that drops or renames in one step (T-183). _Spec: T3 §13, T-48, T-49. Model: opus._
- [x] **1.6 First tables.** `accounts`, `profiles`, `profile_access`, `leagues`, `league_slug_history`, `league_features`, `programs`, `seasons`, `role_grants`, `invitations`, `activity_log`, `support_access_log`, `command_receipts`, with the conventions of T-40 to T-47: `league_id` on every league table and in every link, UUID version 7 keys, UTC times, `deleted_at`, `version`. One default program per league. _Spec: T3 §1–5, §12. Done test: constraint tests for each rule in T3 §12 that applies to these tables. Model: opus._
- [x] **1.7 Row-level security.** A restricted database role for the app (T-60). Policies on every league table keyed to the league set at the start of each transaction (T-61); account-keyed policies for personal tables (T-62). _Spec: T4 §2. Done test: as the restricted role, a query with no league set returns nothing; with league A set, league B's rows are invisible and cannot be written. Model: opus, high._
- [x] **1.8 Typed queries.** Kysely over the schema, types generated from the migrations. Every function that touches league data requires a league ID (T-28). A transaction helper that sets league and account, used by everything. The helper always sets them with `set_config(..., true)`, for that one transaction only, never for the whole session: a pooled connection would otherwise carry one league into the next request. A test proves it: a league set in one transaction is gone in the next one on the same connection. _Spec: T1 §1, T2 §6, T-61. Model: opus._
- [x] **1.9 The two-league test harness.** A harness that creates two leagues and, for every registered command and query, tries league A's access against league B's records; any success fails the gate. New commands are picked up automatically from the registry. _Spec: T-65. Done test: a deliberately leaky command planted in a test is caught. Model: opus, high._ The harness and its case registry live in `packages/database/src/isolation/`; hooking up commands is finished in step 1.10, whose commands add their cases to the same registry and whose command folders join the coverage scan.

### C. Rules of the product

- [x] **1.10 The command shape.** `command(context, input, deps) → result | error` with typed results, typed expected errors, permission check, one transaction, follow-up jobs recorded in the same transaction, and the log line of T-196. Events (T-24). The command registry the harness reads. _Spec: T2 §3, T-23 to T-26, T-74, T-196. Model: opus._
- [x] **1.11 Leagues.** Module `leagues`: create a league (internal tool only for now), short-name rules and the blocked list (U-7), rename with forwarding, states draft, live, archived, suspended (U-9), the hidden default program (U-3, U-12), season records. _Spec: P2 §5–6, T3 §4. Model: sonnet._
- [x] **1.26 Catch up with main.** GitHub's `main` (already here as `origin/main`, commit 24d8bfb) is 8 commits ahead of where this branch started: the game-ready live stats tracker, its Supabase setup and its GitHub Pages site, about 57 files. Bring them in with `git merge origin/main`: no fetch, no push, never a rebase. Where both sides changed a file, keep `main`'s tracker behavior and its tests exactly, and keep this branch's new structure and gate; every test that came from `main` must pass unchanged. `supabase/site.json` names the founder's real Supabase project: nothing in the gate and nothing a run does may contact it (T-201); tests use the fake. If a script would contact it, do not run it and say so in the log. Do it in its own lane and land it with a real merge (`git merge --no-ff`), so the history of `main` is kept. It does not have to be alone: other lanes may be open beside it. _Spec: T-16, T-201. Done test: `git log HEAD..origin/main` prints nothing; `npm run verify` passes. Model: opus, high._
- [x] **1.12 Access.** Module `access`: the fixed roles and their permissions (A-3, O-7), role grants with scope, invitations (create, accept, re-send, cancel, expire), removing access takes effect at once (T-75), the activity log (A-6). A test of every role against every command (T4 §12). _Spec: P4 §4, T4 §4, T3 §5. Model: opus._

### D. Sign-in

- [x] **1.13 The sign-in interface and local stand-in.** An interface in `packages/providers` for: start sign-up with an emailed code, set a password, sign in, sign out, sign out everywhere, list sessions, reset by code. A local stand-in for development and tests only, clearly marked as not for production. _Spec: T-6, T-14, T-67 to T-71, T-85. Model: opus, high._
- [x] **1.14 Sign-in flows in the web app.** Sign up (email, code, password), sign in, forgotten password, Google button behind the interface, the session cookie (T-69), no time limit (T-70), the password again for sensitive actions, the new-device email, the device list with "sign out everywhere" (T-71), identical behavior whether or not an account exists (T-68), attempt limits (T-85). _Spec: P6 §2 and §5, T4 §3. Needs: 1.17, 1.19. Model: opus, high._
- [x] **1.15 The Supabase adapter.** The real adapter for the same interface, unit-tested against recorded responses. Marked not verified against the live service. _Spec: T-5, T-6. Model: opus._

### E. The web app and the worker

- [x] **1.16 Address builder and request context.** One function that builds every league address, and `server/context.ts` as the only place a request becomes "who, which league" (T-34, T4 §2 fence 1). _Model: opus._
- [x] **1.17 Web app shell.** Next.js app in `apps/web` with the folders of T2 §4: our own pages, `[league]` public shell, `[league]/admin` shell with its navigation and empty areas, the tracker route as a placeholder. Typing an admin address without access shows "you do not have access" (U-6). Unpublished leagues are visible only to their admins. _Spec: T2 §4, P2 §4, P4 §3. Model: sonnet._
- [x] **1.18 Design values and message files.** A league's design document turned into CSS variables once per page (T-90); header, menu, footer with the "Powered by SR Leagues" mark (U-8); two visibly different starting designs. All interface text from message files (T-187). Right-to-left text renders correctly (T-188). _Spec: T5 §1, P5 §2. Model: sonnet._
- [x] **1.19 The worker and the queue.** A queue interface with jobs recorded in the same transaction as their cause (T-130), carrying identifiers only (T-131), safe to run twice (T-137). The pg-boss adapter for real PostgreSQL. If pg-boss cannot run against PGlite, write the decision record and use a small table-backed stand-in for local work and tests behind the same interface. An email interface with a capture adapter, so no email leaves the machine (T-140), and the Resend adapter unverified. One real job: the invitation email. _Spec: T7 §1 and §5–6, T-7, T-11. Model: opus._
- [x] **1.20 Logging and errors.** Structured logs with a request ID (T-196), no personal content (T-86), an error-reporting interface with a local adapter and the Sentry adapter unverified. A health check for web and worker. _Spec: T8 §7, T4 §10. Model: sonnet._

### F. Proving it

- [x] **1.21 Seed leagues.** Two made-up leagues with different designs, admins and members, loaded by one command. No real people. _Spec: T-195. Model: haiku._
- [ ] **1.22 Browser tests for the exit test.** In a real browser: two leagues at two addresses with different looks; a person signs in, closes the browser, returns and is still signed in; an admin of the first is refused everywhere in the second; an invitation email is captured and its link works. Accessibility checks on each screen (T-186). How it runs (decided by the lead on 2026-11-14, after two runs skipped this step for want of a browser): the tests use the `playwright` package this repository already has, against the web app on its made-up stand-in, started the way `scripts/preview-web.mjs` starts it. On this computer they open the browser Windows already has (`chromium.launch({ channel: 'msedge' })`, tried and working), so nothing is downloaded or installed. On GitHub's machines, which are the judge, they run in the Chromium that `.github/workflows/ci.yml` already installs: add the new script there after the other browser checks and leave every other line of that file alone. _Spec: T10 stage 1, T9 §2. Folders: `tests/browser`, `scripts`, `package.json`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Model: sonnet._
- [x] **1.23 CI.** The GitHub workflow runs the new gate. Nothing is pushed by a run; this only edits the file. _Model: haiku._
- [ ] **1.24 Records.** A decision record for each choice in T1 that stage 1 used, and for every decision made along the way. `docs/operations/` gets "run it locally" and "apply migrations". _Spec: T9 §5. Model: haiku to draft, lead to check._
- [ ] **1.27 Sturdy timing tests.** Three of the last twelve checks on GitHub failed and then passed on the next commit with no fix in between, and the log names the same tests failing on this computer under load and passing alone. Make them wait for the thing they test instead of for a length of time: `packages/database/src/migrations/run-migrations.test.ts` ('waits for another run holding the lock'), `tests/live-stats-server.test.mjs` (reads the server's start-up text too early) and `tests/live-stats-*.test.mjs` (hosted backup), and the 'Timeout calling onTaskUpdate' and 90-second limits seen in the isolation tests. Change how a test waits, never what it checks: no assertion is removed or loosened, no test is skipped, and nothing under `apps/live-stats` or `packages/sports` changes. Also part of this step since 2026-11-14 (the lead): `scripts/check-pages-browser.mjs`, whose fixed waits of 15 to 30 seconds fail about one GitHub run in eight. Make it wait for what it tests, changing no check and nothing under `apps/live-stats`. Prove the whole step on GitHub's machines, where the gate runs now: one commit passes the whole check five times in a row (push it to `lane/1.27-again1` to `lane/1.27-again5`, read them with `node scripts/github-check.mjs`, then delete them). _Needs: nothing. Migration: no. Folders: `tests`, `packages/database/src/migrations`, `packages/database/src/isolation`, `vitest.config.ts`, `scripts/check-pages-browser.mjs`. Done test: five green runs of one commit on GitHub as described, and the diff shows no changed or removed assertion. Model: sonnet, medium. Job: checks._

- [ ] **1.25 Whole-stage review and report.** As in the runbook, section 7. The report's founder checklist includes at least: turn on two-step sign-in for the business accounts (T-83); create the Supabase, Render, Cloudflare and Resend accounts and a domain; set up the shared password vault (T-166); then one supervised session to connect staging, switch on continuous backup, ship a release and reverse it. _Model: opus, xhigh._

## Side by side

What each remaining step needs before its lane can be opened (runbook, sections 2 and 3). A step with "nothing new" can be opened now. Several steps are built in two parts so the first part does not wait; each part lands as its own commit, and the step is ticked when both have landed.

| Step                                  | Needs                                                           | Migration | Notes                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1.26 Catch up with main               | nothing new                                                     | no        | Lands with a real merge, not a squash. Other lanes may be open beside it; each takes it in when it catches up before landing.       |
| 1.12 Access                           | 1.11 (landed)                                                   | no        | Tables exist since 1.6. If it finds it needs a table change, it asks the lead for a migration number.                               |
| 1.13 Sign-in interface and stand-in   | nothing new                                                     | no        | `packages/providers`.                                                                                                               |
| 1.15 Supabase adapter                 | 1.13                                                            | no        |                                                                                                                                     |
| 1.16 Address builder, request context | 1.13                                                            | no        | The address builder half needs nothing new and can go first.                                                                        |
| 1.17 Web app shell                    | 1.12, 1.16                                                      | no        |                                                                                                                                     |
| 1.18 Design values and message files  | part 1: nothing new · part 2: 1.17                              | no        | Part 1: design document to CSS variables, the message-file loader, right-to-left. Part 2: header, menu and footer inside the shell. |
| 1.19 Worker and queue                 | part 1: nothing new · part 2: 1.12                              | yes       | Part 1: queue and email interfaces, stand-ins, adapters, the jobs table. Part 2: the invitation email job.                          |
| 1.20 Logging and errors               | part 1: nothing new · part 2: 1.17 and 1.19                     | no        | Part 1: the logging and error-reporting library. Part 2: the health checks for web and worker.                                      |
| 1.14 Sign-in flows in the web app     | 1.13, 1.17, 1.19                                                | maybe     | Sessions and attempt limits may need tables: reserve a migration number.                                                            |
| 1.21 Seed leagues                     | 1.12, 1.18 part 1                                               | no        |                                                                                                                                     |
| 1.23 CI                               | 1.26                                                            | no        | The workflow file changes when `main` is merged in, so this waits for it.                                                           |
| 1.22 Browser tests                    | 1.14, 1.17, 1.18, 1.19, 1.21                                    | no        |                                                                                                                                     |
| 1.24 Records                          | drafts: nothing new · final pass: everything else in this table | no        | A decision record is written by the lane that makes the decision. This step fills the gaps and writes the two operations guides.    |
| 1.27 Sturdy timing tests              | nothing                                                         | no        | Tests only. Open it early: every failed check costs a run and holds `main` back.                                                    |
| 1.25 Whole-stage review and report    | every other step                                                | no        | Alone for this stage: no lane of stage 1 open. Lanes of later stages may carry on.                                                  |

So right now six lanes can be open: 1.26, 1.12, 1.13, and the first parts of 1.18, 1.19 and 1.20. When stage 1 has fewer steps that can be opened than there are lanes, the spare lanes take steps from [stage 2](STAGE-2.md) that need only what has already landed.

## What stage 1 cannot finish without the founder

Staging and production, the release and reverse-release rehearsal, continuous backup, uptime checks, real Google sign-in and real email all need vendor accounts. Everything up to them is built and tested locally in this stage. They become the founder's checklist in the stage report, and stage 1 is called done only after that supervised session.
